tasks.title: Implement RetentionSweeper background task with 7-day DELETE logic and WAL checkpoint
tasks.description: Implement server/app/audit_log/retention.py with the RetentionSweeper class. The sweeper runs as an asyncio background task launched from lifespan(). It loops every AUDIT_RETENTION_SWEEP_INTERVAL_HOURS hours. On each tick it calls AuditStore.cleanup_expired(retention_days) which issues DELETE FROM <table> WHERE created_at < datetime('now', '-? days') on all four time-stamped tables: classifications, agent_traces, alerts, conversations. After the sweep it optionally runs PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE) if AUDIT_VACUUM_ON_RETENTION=true. On any exception: log ERROR, increment metric, continue loop.
acceptance_criteria: RetentionSweeper class exists in server/app/audit_log/retention.py with start() and stop() async methods
cleanup_expired(7) deletes rows older than exactly 7 days from all four tables (classifications, agent_traces, alerts, conversations)
cleanup_expired() returns total rows deleted as int (sum across all tables)
After exception in sweep: task loop continues; next sweep runs at next interval without restart
audit_retention_rows_deleted_total counter increments by the returned int after each sweep
audit_retention_sweep_complete log event emits rows_deleted and sweep_duration_ms
WAL checkpoint runs after sweep when AUDIT_VACUUM_ON_RETENTION=true

tasks.title: Implement conversations table write and read_conversation_history API for Context Agent
tasks.description: Implement record_conversation_turn() and read_conversation_history() in SqliteAuditStore. record_conversation_turn() inserts one row into the conversations table and auto-increments turn_index per child_id using MAX(turn_index)+1. read_conversation_history(child_id, last_n_turns=5) issues SELECT ... ORDER BY turn_index DESC LIMIT n and returns a list[ConversationTurn] sorted oldest-first (reversed in Python). This resolves review.md G-01 open question Q4 — the Context Agent's read_history tool reads from this table, not from the agent_traces table which only stores borderline cases.

tasks.title: Implement failure-mode fallbacks per LLD §8 (locked DB, disk full, schema migration failure)
tasks.description: Implement the four failure modes documented in LLD §8 inside SqliteAuditStore and the lifespan() composition root. (1) SQLite locked: exponential backoff retry 3× (50ms / 150ms / 450ms); on 3rd failure log ERROR and drop write — classification response is still returned. (2) Disk full: lifespan() catches OperationalError on the next write attempt; switches app.state.audit from SqliteAuditStore to NullAuditStore; /health returns degraded. (3) Schema migration failure on startup: init() raises — let it propagate so lifespan() fails and the server does not start (fail-fast). (4) Retention sweep error: log ERROR, increment metric, continue loop.
acceptance_criteria: Simulating sqlite3.OperationalError('database is locked') on first write attempt: SqliteAuditStore retries with 50ms backoff and succeeds on retry
Simulating 3 consecutive lock errors: classification response is returned normally; audit row is missing; audit_db_write_errors_total{reason='sqlite_locked'} increments by 3
Simulating disk-full OperationalError: app.state.audit is replaced with NullAuditStore; /health returns {'status': 'degraded', 'audit_log_writable': false}
Simulating corrupt migration (DROP TABLE classifications before init()): SqliteAuditStore.init() raises; server startup fails with a CRITICAL log line; server does not accept requests
Simulating exception in RetentionSweeper._run_loop(): loop continues; next sweep fires at next interval; audit_db_write_errors_total{reason='retention_sweep'} increments
